svg.aria-label: Chroma keying as a region on the Cb Cr plane
svg.text: Chroma keying is a shape drawn on the Cb/Cr plane
Drop Y' and 'is this pixel screen or subject?' stops being a colour question and becomes plane geometry.
Two ways to draw the same intention
Brighten the screen and every pixel slides outward along
this line. The angle is the hue and it barely moves - 2.5
degrees across three stops. The radius is just exposure.
Plain distance from the key colour. What ffmpeg's chromakey
does. Has to be widened until it swallows the darkest corner
of the screen, and widening is what starts eating foreground.
Angle from the key hue, with a saturation floor. Indifferent
to how the screen is lit. This is what real keyers do.
Hair, motion blur, smoke and glass all live in the middle band. Widen it and
edges soften; close it and you get a cut-out with jagged edges.
The green jumper sits 16 degrees from the key hue, just outside both regions. That one degree of margin is the whole reason nobody wears
green on a green screen. Dark hair, by the way, lands almost exactly on neutral grey - which is why it keys cleanly and shadows do not.
